summary: SAML c14n strict-mode rejects encapsulated AttributeValue from customer IdP, preventing private-console login
description: Issue summary: Customer FinovatePay reports users cannot access the Redwood Private admin console after IdP-initiated SSO. The SAML response is accepted but attribute-based role resolution fails, leading to 403 'insufficient privileges' on console load. Impact: All customer admins are unable to perform org-level actions (console, user provisioning). Time window: started ~2026-03-11 08:04 UTC and persistent. This ticket covers investigation and remediation.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer initiates SAML SSO from their IdP (IdP-initiated login) to Redwood Private console
2) IdP sends SAML Response with Attribute elements containing AttributeValue nodes where values are xml-encapsulated (IdP wraps attribute contents using additional namespace/payload),
3) Identity-proxy verifies signature and forwards assertion to auth service
4) Auth service performs canonicalization using strict SAML C14N path and then runs attribute-to-role mapping -> user receives no role bindings and console returns 403
expected_behavior: Attributes should be canonicalized in a permissive mode that preserves encapsulated text content for role mapping. Admin role bindings should be populated from the 'roles' AttributeValue and access granted.
actual_behavior: AttributeValue elements that contain nested namespaced XML are dropped during canonicalization/normalization step. Role resolution yields empty set; token issued with no admin roles resulting in 403 on console.
logs: identity-proxy: WARN 2026-03-11T08:04:12Z c14n: strict mode removed text node inside AttributeValue for Attribute 'roles' length before=1 after=0 assertion_id=xyz-assert-789
auth-service: ERROR 2026-03-11T08:04:13Z rbac: no role bindings found for principal=finovatepay|user:alice@example.com
investigation_notes: 2026-03-11 09:00 UTC - Support triage: reproduced against a debug proxy using customer-provided SAML Response sample. Observed c14n behavior differs when AttributeValue contains nested namespace-qualified XML elements (e.g., <meta:data>value</meta:data>)

2026-03-11 11:30 UTC - SRE: identity-proxy enforces canonicalization configured to 'strict' mode for SAML assertions as of release 2025-12-02. This setting removed text nodes inside unknown namespaced children under AttributeValue during c14n pass.

2026-03-11 13:00 UTC - Customer notes: Upstream IdP began packaging role attributes as small XML fragments to support localized metadata injection last week (change request ID idp-942). This is the first time we see interaction with Redwood c14n.

2026-03-11 14:10 UTC - Hypothesis: strict c14n implementation in identity-proxy canonicalizes children nodes in a way that drops text nodes inside nested namespaced elements when not in a whitelist. That results in empty AttributeValue payloads post-normalization.

2026-03-12 08:45 UTC - Test: toggling identity-proxy to permissive-c14n for a single tenant in staging restores attribute payload and GC -> role resolution succeeds. Attached test assertion: saml_response_test_586420.xml

2026-03-12 10:20 UTC - Security review: permissive vs strict c14n tradeoffs considered. Permissive allows more IdP encodings but increases surface when parsing untrusted XML. Customer is enterprise with private deployment and HSM-backed signature verification in place; risk accepted with scoped change.
comments: Support (Riley Chen) 2026-03-11T09:05 UTC: Thanks FinovatePay for the SAML sample. We're reproducing locally and investigating canonicalization path. Slack thread: #support-finovatepay (https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C0123ABC)

Customer (FinovatePay - Elena Martin) 2026-03-11T10:12 UTC: We pushed a change last week to include a <meta:locale> wrapper around role values for downstream services. Happy to test any changes you propose.
SRE (Mateo Ruiz) 2026-03-11T11:40 UTC: Confirmed identity-proxy c14n behavior. Short-term workaround: we can enable tenant-scoped permissive canonicalization. Will need ops approval for prod change.

Security (Anika Shah) 2026-03-11T15:02 UTC: Reviewed risk. For a private enterprise tenant with mutual TLS and signed assertions, scoped permissive c14n is acceptable as temporary mitigation. We'll require a code fix to properly preserve encapsulated text nodes while validating signature integrity.
Support (Riley Chen) 2026-03-12T12:00 UTC: Customer tested staging toggle; reported success: console access restored for admin users. Awaiting ops window for prod change and engineering fix.
resolution_notes: Temporary mitigation: enabled tenant-scoped 'permissive-c14n' in identity-proxy for FinovatePay on 2026-03-12 18:00 UTC which restored role parsing and admin access. Permanent fix: engineering to release identity-proxy patch that preserves encapsulated AttributeValue text nodes while maintaining signature validation (PR #4815). Planned rollout to prod: 2026-03-16. Postmortem checklist: update SAML onboarding docs to call out allowed AttributeValue encodings, add a diagnostic that logs AttributeValue length pre/post-c14n for tenant debug, and add an automated test with namespaced encapsulated AttributeValue samples.
next_steps: 1) Engineer (Mateo Ruiz) to merge PR #4815 and coordinate canary rollout (target 2026-03-16).
2) Ops to monitor role-mapping metrics and error rate for FinovatePay following canary (alert on >5% role resolution failures).
3) Support to notify customer of deployment schedule and confirm post-deploy validation steps.
4) Docs: update SAML onboarding guide with example of acceptable encodings and contact points for preflight tests.
